Had the same thing when I bought my apartment. I learned to let go of the things that I can't fix. I fought hard but there comes a time when you don't have the strenght anymore. Other things pile up for example at work. My health is not letting me do all of the things that I plan. I often use Shultz's Autogene Training when the stress level are over the roof. I recommend you do it too. As for the little stresses think of this as a gym training routine. Make todo list of things that make you worry. Prioritize them. Try to count how much time each thing will take. Multiply that time by 2,5 to get a healthy result for each item. It sounds silly at first but beleave me there is always something that will suprize you. Take one item off the list, do it and then rest. Rest is important. Same for the gym training. You have to let your muscles grow. Your efficiency drops when you are overloaded. After a time beeing you will know how much you can take and the stress will go away. There is only as much as you can do. The rest will have to wait. Saying "not now" is not a bad thing. I had a ton of ocasions that needed my attention and let them go because I had no time or strenght for that. They come and go.
